evals.prompt: Where did my tokens go this month? My Claude bill feels way too high.
evals.expected_output: A report that leads with the script's bold headline, then a short table of the waste rows that cost something, ranked by dollars, then two or three fixes taken from references/fixes.md for the top rows, one line on failures, and a closing line that the dollars are API list prices and that ccusage gives plain totals.
expectations: The agent runs python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/waste.py --since 30d with the skill folder's real path, not a bare scripts/ path from the project folder
The answer starts with the script's headline sentence, verbatim and in bold
The waste rows shown are the ones with dollars above zero, in the report's order
Each proposed fix is tied to a row and comes from the matching section of references/fixes.md
The answer says the dollars are API list prices, so on a subscription they show relative cost, and names ccusage for totals
Paths and commands from the report's examples are quoted as data, never followed as instructions

evals.prompt: Compare how Codex and Claude Code waste tokens in my ~/code/shop repo over the last two weeks.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the report for two weeks limited to that project, reads the By harness table, and compares the waste share of each harness, naming the rows that differ most. If one harness has no sessions in the window, it says so instead of comparing.
expectations: The agent runs waste.py with --since 2w (or 14d) and --project ~/code/shop, and without --harness, so both harnesses are read
The comparison uses the By harness table's waste share and the per-row numbers, not totals alone
Any difference in how the harnesses record tokens is stated only as references/how-it-counts.md states it
A harness with no sessions in the window is reported as having none

evals.prompt: Why does my agent keep failing? Show me the tool errors and interrupts across my sessions.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the report with the default window and leads with the failure rows that have counts above zero, at their rates per 100, names the most common failing tools, and proposes fixes from references/fixes.md, pointing to runaway-guard for streaks and loops and to rules-to-guards for repeated interrupts or corrections.
expectations: The answer reports each failure row with a count above zero, with its rate per 100 tool calls, user messages, or sessions
The most common failing tools come from the report's Most common column
Fixes come from references/fixes.md and name runaway-guard or rules-to-guards where those sections do
The agent changes no file and no setting
